messages.text: I keep my eyes open for trouble.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Old iron rings are set into the walls. Dust and damp mix into a sour smell.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I drink a little water and pass the skin along.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Your footsteps echo off the wet stone. The day wears on.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I ask how much farther we have to go.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Somewhere below, water is moving. The stair winds down into the dark.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I ask the others what they think of all this.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Ripples spread from every movement. Drowned shelves lean under the surface.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I drink a little water and pass the skin along.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Echoes carry strangely across the hall. You share a quiet meal.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I ask the others what they think of all this.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: The floodwater in the hall tastes of copper and stings the cuts on your hands.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I ask how much farther we have to go.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Something brushes past under the water. Time passes slowly.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I keep my eyes open for trouble.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Ripples spread from every movement. Pillars march away into the flooded dark.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I look back the way we came.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: A drowned statue rises from the water, and its plinth names it Queen Amarante.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I check my pack and tighten the straps.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Your breath fogs in the cold air. The others rest while you keep watch.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I offer to take the next watch.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: You cross the hall in a reed coracle found tied to a pillar.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Pale eels the old archivists called glasstongues circle beneath the surface.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: From a high shelf you recover the book you came for, the Ledger of Tides.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I keep my eyes open for trouble.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: The chamber smells of old vellum. A joke passes along the line and earns a tired laugh.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I look back the way we came.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Ink stains cover the long table. The others rest while you keep watch.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I rest for a moment and catch my breath.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: The keeper of the archive gives his name as Absalom, and says he has waited a long time.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I drink a little water and pass the skin along.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Shadows sway as the candle flames move. You share a quiet meal.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I keep one hand on my knife.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Ink stains cover the long table. Candles burn in niches all around the chamber.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I nod and keep walking.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Pages turn somewhere in the dark without a hand to turn them. The chamber smells of old vellum.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I rest for a moment and catch my breath.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: His price for letting you leave is a lock of hair, cut with his own silver knife.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I drink a little water and pass the skin along.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: The keeper speaks in a voice as dry as paper. Books are stacked to the ceiling in crooked towers.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I study the faces around me.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I ask the others what they think of all this.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: He warns you never to sail under a red moon, or the archive will call you back.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I keep close to the others and watch the road.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Pages turn somewhere in the dark without a hand to turn them. A clock with no hands ticks on the wall.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I help lift a heavy load.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: A clock with no hands ticks on the wall. You check your gear again.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I nod and keep walking.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: The great tide, he says, will come at dawn of the seventh day.

messages.speaker: Player
messages.text: I stay quiet and listen.

arrival.speaker: Narrator
arrival.text: At last the tunnel opens onto the shore, and you smell the sea. The boats wait on the sand, and the tide is turning.
